subject: Regional hosting & keystore operator — operational evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medisys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Walker <tom.walker@medisys.com>, security@medisys.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Operational proof for US hosting + keystore operator details

Priya —

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of our procurement checklist for Medisys’ pilot, we need a short operational packet confirming two things for the US-hosted deployment: 1) that hosting and private endpoints for our tenancy are physically in the US (no cross-border egress by design), and 2) the keystore/operator model — specifically who can access HSM/KMS key material, how operator access is separated, and the rotation plan.

Can you provide the minimal artifacts we can consume in our vendor-security review? A simple CSV roster of operator roles, a one-page rotation plan summary, and any SOC 2 snapshot that references key management practices would be perfect.

We’d like those by EOD next Tuesday (20 Jan) to stay on our procurement timeline. If anything needs approvals, please flag.

Appreciate it —
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security Ops
Medisys Health

Attachments: none
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medisys.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Operational proof for US hosting + keystore operator details

Marcus / Jonas —

Medisys is asking for a concise evidence packet: US-only hosting confirmation + operator roster and a rotation summary for keystores. Elena asked for a CSV roster, a one-page rotation plan, and a SOC 2 snapshot referencing KMS practice by 20 Jan.

Can you pull the following and drop into a single zip:
- medisys_keystore_operator_roster.csv (operator, role, region, access_type, date_provisioned)
- operator-keystore-rotation-plan.pdf (1p executive summary + link to runbook)
- soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf (excerpt of KMS/crypto controls)
- privatelink-egress-matrix.csv (shows egress paths are US-only for the tenant)

Jonas: please confirm whether the keystore is split across operator groups (support vs. infra) and whether we rely on blinded-sign or HSM-backed unwrap. Marcus: can you export the roster and include timestamps and the last rotation event?

If there are compliance redlines (e.g., third-party operator access), call them out. I’ll stitch and send to Medisys.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medisys.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Operational proof for US hosting + keystore operator details

Priya / Jonas —

I extracted operator data and drafted the rotation summary. Quick notes:
- The keystore is HSM-backed (cloud KMS with customer-key partitioning). No third-party operator has persistent unwrapped-key access.
- Operator roles are split: "Infra-Operator" (in-cloud infra ops, ability to create key versions under scoped roles) and "Support-Observer" (read-only audit access). Emergency unseal is an approval flow that is multi-party and logged.
- Last scheduled rotation: 2025-11-03 (automated rewrap + manual key-switch for master wrap).

I attached the CSV and a one-page PDF summary. I’ll also add the privacy of egress matrix to show US-only endpoints for the Medisys tenancy.

Attachments: medisys_keystore_operator_roster.csv (CSV, 12KB); operator-keystore-rotation-plan.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Marcus Lin
Platform Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medisys.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Operational proof for US hosting + keystore operator details

Priya / Elena —

Confirming a couple implementation specifics for the packet:
- Hosting: tenant nodes for the Medisys pilot are pinned to the us-east-1 and us-west-2 regions; routing policy blocks cross-region replication for customer data by default. I’ve exported a short privatelink-egress-matrix.csv that maps service endpoints and netblocks to those regions.
- Keystore: we use cloud HSM with customer keys stored in tenant-specific partitions. Operator access is RBAC-controlled via our internal IAM; operators do not have direct console unwrap permissions — only a signed workflow that creates a short-lived ephemeral unlock token audited by the vault.
- CAIQ/SIG pointers: we can include CAIQ answers for key management; SOC 2 snapshot included will be the controls that reference encryption and key rotation.

I attached the egress matrix and a small example runbook excerpt for the emergency unwrap approval flow.

Attachments: privatelink-egress-matrix.csv (CSV, 7KB); runbook-unlock-excerpt.txt (TXT, 4KB)

Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medisys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Operational proof for US hosting + keystore operator details

Elena —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is the compiled evidence packet for Medisys: compiled-evidence-packet.zip. Contents (summary):
- medisys_keystore_operator_roster.csv — operator, role, region, access_type, date_provisioned, last_rotation_event
- operator-keystore-rotation-plan.pdf — 1-page executive summary + reference to internal runbook (locked); included short rotation timeline
- soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf — excerpt (control IDs included) referencing KMS handling and encryption-in-transit/rest
- privatelink-egress-matrix.csv — mapping of private endpoints and netblocks showing US-only egress path for the tenancy
- runbook-unlock-excerpt.txt — redacted sample of emergency unseal approval flow (audit logging highlighted)

Links: drive folder with the packet (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-keystore-evidence). For intake tracking I created SECOPS-442.

Callouts:
- There is no persistent human access to unwrapped key material; emergency procedures require 3 approvers and produce an immutable audit trail.
- If Medisys needs CAIQ answer export instead of the SOC 2 excerpt, we can generate the CAIQ Key Mgmt section (will take 48 hours).

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of this packet or list any gaps by EOD Friday 23 Jan so procurement can proceed.

Best —
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compiled-evidence-packet.zip (ZIP, 1.2MB)
